extracted.intended_audience: users of GAP (computational group theorists / mathematicians) who create, manipulate, and simplify finitely presented groups and subgroup presentations using Tietze transformations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and command-level rules for creating, printing, transforming, simplifying, and obtaining subgroup/normal-closure presentations in GAP using Tietze transformations, Reidemeister–Schreier and Todd–Coxeter methods. Focuses on when/how to apply operations and how options affect results.

rubrics_metrics.name: printLevel option semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tietze option printLevel controls messages displayed by Tietze transformation commands: default value 1 is for interactive use and implies explicit messages; value 0 suppresses messages; value 2 enforces additional output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set printLevel to 0 to suppress messages in batch jobs; use 2 to get extra verbose output during interactive simplification and debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzSort behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: TzSort(P) sorts the relators of presentation P by increasing lengths. No particular ordering is defined for relators of equal length. TzSort mutates the given presentation (does not return a new object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to reorder relators prior to running Tietze routines that assume or benefit from relators sorted by length.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfPresentation returns shallow copy
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfPresentation(P) returns a list of free generators that is a shallow copy of the current generators of presentation P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware names returned are display figures — to use them as variables you must assign them (introduce variables and assign gens[i] to them).

rubrics_metrics.name: FpGroupPresentation constructs f.p. group from Tietze presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: FpGroupPresentation(P[, nam]) constructs a finitely presented (fp) group as defined by the given Tietze presentation P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting group is the group defined by the presentation; equality of groups can be tested but may be false if different internal representations are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: PresentationViaCosetTable algorithm and two-stage option
rubrics_metrics.description: PresentationViaCosetTable(G[, F, words]) constructs a presentation for a concrete finite group using a relations-finding algorithm and automatically applies Tietze transformations. If only G is specified, a single-stage algorithm is applied; supplying a subgroup H as F and words triggers a two-stage algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-stage algorithm saves space by constructing two coset tables of lengths |H| and |G|/|H| instead of one of length |G|. Before returning, the resulting presentation is simplified but WITHOUT eliminating generators, preserving a bijection between group generators and presentation generators. If you don't require that bijection, call SimplifyPresentation again (allowing eliminations) to get a shorter presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SimplifiedFpGroup purpose and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: SimplifiedFpGroup(G) applies Tietze transformations to a copy of G's presentation to reduce number of generators, relators, and relator lengths and returns an isomorphic group with a (tried-to-be) simplified presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsomorphismSimplifiedFpGroup should be used if you need the isomorphism. If result unsatisfying, use interactive Tietze commands for more sophisticated strategies. The procedure P := PresentationFpGroup(G,0); SimplifyPresentation(P); H := FpGroupPresentation(P) describes the usual sequence applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: PresentationSubgroupRrs (Reduced Reidemeister–Schreier)
rubrics_metrics.description: PresentationSubgroupRrs(G, H[, string] or G, table[, string]) uses the Reduced Reidemeister–Schreier method to compute a presentation P for a subgroup H of a finitely presented group G. Generators in the resulting presentation are named string1, string2, ... (default '_x').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only H is given, PresentationSubgroupRrs first obtains a coset table. It constructs a set of primary subgroup generators (smaller but possibly redundant) and then introduces many secondary subgroup generators as abbreviations to keep word lengths short; finally a Reidemeister rewriting yields relators for H. The returned presentation generally needs further simplification via Tietze transformations or DecodeTree before being compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimaryGeneratorWords attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimaryGeneratorWords(P) is an attribute of presentation P that holds a list of words in the associated group generators which express the primary subgroup generators of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this attribute to get the expressions of primary subgroup generators as words in the parent group's generators; useful when you need the connection between subgroup and group generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: PresentationSubgroupMtc (Modified Todd–Coxeter) behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: PresentationSubgroupMtc(G, H[, string][, print, level]) uses the Modified Todd–Coxeter method to compute a presentation for H. The result is in generators corresponding to generators of H. Default print level is 1; print level 0 suppresses DecodeTree output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Method builds an augmented coset table with correction elements (subgroup elements). It introduces many secondary generators (redundant abbreviations) so words remain short, then uses a decoding tree algorithm to eliminate secondary generators providing a presentation on the primary generators. Decoding tree may add many intermediate generators/relators and can even change the isomorphism type; you are strongly recommended to read section 48.10 and to try additional Tietze simplification afterward. For some subgroups RRS may give more concise presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PresentationNormalClosureRrs is RRS for normal closure
rubrics_metrics.description: PresentationNormalClosureRrs(G, H[, string]) uses the Reduced Reidemeister–Schreier method to compute a presentation for the normal closure of subgroup H in G. Generators are named as string1, string2, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PresentationNormalClosure is a synonym for PresentationNormalClosureRrs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal relator representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Internally, each relator is represented by a list of positive or negative generator numbers (position numbers relative to the current list of generators) rather than by abstract words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering of generators in Tietze words is always relative to the generator list and bears no relation to internal numbering in other word families; this representation speeds Tietze routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: TietzeWordAbstractWord conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: TietzeWordAbstractWord(word, fgens) converts an abstract word in the given free generators to a Tietze word (list of signed generator numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This function simply calls LetterRepAssocWord; use when constructing Tietze-word-format relators programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbstractWordTietzeWord conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: AbstractWordTietzeWord(word, fgens) converts a Tietze word (signed generator-number list) back to an abstract word in the given free generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This function calls AssocWordByLetterRep; useful for readable output of Tietze-internal relators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default printing of presentations and special print commands
rubrics_metrics.description: When a presentation P is created or assigned, GAP prints a one-line summary (number of generators, number of relators, total relator length) to avoid verbose output. Special TzPrint* commands provide detailed views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TzPrintGenerators, TzPrintRelators, TzPrintStatus, TzPrintPresentation, TzPrint, and TzPrintPairs for controlled detailed output. TzPrintOptions controls printing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrintGenerators behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrintGenerators(P[, list]) prints the generators of presentation P together with the number of their occurrences in the relators. Optional second argument restricts which generator numbers to print (default: all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to identify rarely/never occurring generators (candidates for elimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrintRelators behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrintRelators(P[, list]) prints the relators of P. Optional argument list selects relators to print (default: all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after simplification steps to inspect current relators in abstract-word form.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrintLengths behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrintLengths(P) prints a list of all relator lengths of presentation P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick diagnostic of relator-length distribution; useful before/after TzSearch/TzEliminate.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrintStatus behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrintStatus(P[, norepeat]) prints number of generators, number of relators, and total length of relators. If norepeat=true, printing is suppressed if none of these values changed since the last call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used internally by Tietze routines to summarize progress; useful for monitoring changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrintPresentation abbreviation
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrintPresentation(P) prints generators and relators and status; it is an abbreviation for TzPrintGenerators, TzPrintRelators, and TzPrintStatus called successively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient single-call for full presentational printout.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrint behaviour (Tietze words)
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrint(P[, list]) prints the current generators and the relators of P as Tietze words (signed generator-number lists) rather than converting them back to abstract words. Optional list selects relators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want to inspect or manipulate relators in Tietze internal representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzPrintPairs usage and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: TzPrintPairs(P[, n]) prints the n most often occurring relator subwords of the form ab (a and b different generators or inverses) and their occurrence counts. Default n = 10; n = 0 interpreted as infinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when selecting length-2 subwords to substitute as new generators (see TzSubstitute).

rubrics_metrics.name: AddGenerator behaviour and access pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: AddGenerator(P) extends presentation P by a new abstract generator xi with name '_xi' (i is smallest unused positive integer). The new generator can be accessed via P!.i or via Last(GeneratorsOfPresentation(P)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AddGenerator is the public API for adding generators; it maintains necessary global lists (unlike internal TzNewGenerator).

rubrics_metrics.name: TzNewGenerator is internal (do not call)
rubrics_metrics.description: TzNewGenerator(P) is an internal function that defines a new abstract generator and adds it to presentation P. It does not keep global lists consistent and therefore should not be called by users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call AddGenerator instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: AddRelator may change group
rubrics_metrics.description: AddRelator(P, word) adds relator word (an abstract word in P's generators) to presentation P and may change the group defined by P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with care; adding relations changes the defined quotient group.

rubrics_metrics.name: RemoveRelator may change group
rubrics_metrics.description: RemoveRelator(P, n) removes the n-th relator from presentation P and may change the group defined by P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing relators enlarges the defined group; use cautiously when trying variants of presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tietze transformation objective and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tietze transformation commands aim to simplify a presentation by reducing number of generators and relators without increasing too much the total relator length. There is no general algorithm to find the shortest possible presentation; GAP provides lower-level transformation commands and higher-level default strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect that different strategies/options yield different results. For difficult cases, interactive/specialized choices outperform the automatic default strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzGo default automated Tietze strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: TzGo(P[, silent]) automatically performs suitable Tietze transformations on P using a default strategy; it is the most convenient interactive Tietze command. If silent=true, status-line printing by TzGo is suppressed when printLevel < 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TzGo as the primary automatic simplifier; set printLevel and other TzOptions to control behaviour and verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: SimplifyPresentation synonym
rubrics_metrics.description: SimplifyPresentation(P) is a synonym for TzGo(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use either name; examples use SimplifyPresentation as a user-facing simplification routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzGo internal loop and phases
rubrics_metrics.description: TzGo consists of a loop with two phases: search phase (calls TzSearch and TzSearchEqual to reduce relator lengths via substitutions) and elimination phase (calls TzEliminate to eliminate generators expressible as words in remaining generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TzGo prints new status when it reduces number of generators, relators, or total length. If no change is detected it may be useful to repeat TzGo or call TzGoGo (which repeats until no further reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: TzGoGo repeats TzGo until fixed point
rubrics_metrics.description: TzGoGo(P) calls TzGo repeatedly until it no longer reduces the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to exhaust the default automated simplification strategy; results can vary significantly with TzOptions parameters like eliminationsLimit and saveLimit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options influence on TzGo (eliminationsLimit, saveLimit, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tietze option parameters (e.g., eliminationsLimit, saveLimit, printLevel, saveLimit) strongly influence the performance and the final result of TzGo/TzGoGo. Examples show final numbers of generators/relators/total lengths can vary widely with these parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with eliminationsLimit and saveLimit to find better simplifications for concrete problems; do not assume defaults always give best result.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzEliminate elimination criterion and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: TzEliminate(P[, gen] or P[, n] or P[, n]) tries to eliminate a generator from P by substituting a generator that occurs exactly once in some relator with the appropriate word in remaining generators. If multiple candidates exist it chooses the generator minimizing (occurrences × length of substituting word). It will only eliminate if resulting total relator length does not exceed Tietze option spaceLimit (default infinity) or lengthLimit depending on call form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gen specified it attempts to eliminate that generator (only if a relator exists with gen occurring once). If integer n specified, it attempts to eliminate up to n generators. TzEliminate(P) equals TzEliminate(P,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: TzSearch substitution criterion and algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: TzSearch(P) searches for relator subwords where a short relator r1 and a longer relator r2 share a maximal subword w of length greater than l1/2 (possibly after inversion/conjugation); it substitutes each copy of w in r2 by the inverse complement of w in r1 to reduce relators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance and results are influenced by Tietze options saveLimit and searchSimultaneous. saveLimit (default 10%) controls whether another outer loop is started only if the last loop reduced total relator length by at least that percent. searchSimultaneous (default 20) bounds the number of short relators handled concurrently for efficiency trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzSearchEqual substitution for equal complements
rubrics_metrics.description: TzSearchEqual(P) searches for relator subwords where in some relator the complement has equal length (l = l1/2) and substitutes copies of the common subword w in other relators by the inverse complement when appropriate. For l > l1/2 behaves like TzSearch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TzSearchEqual uses searchSimultaneous as TzSearch does but does not use saveLimit; the loop over relators is executed exactly once.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzFindCyclicJoins elimination of cyclic pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: TzFindCyclicJoins(P) searches for power and commutator relators to find pairs of generators that generate a common cyclic subgroup. If it finds [a,b], a^n, and a^s b^t with s prime to n, it uses the Euclidean algorithm to express a as a power of b and then eliminates a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to detect and eliminate redundant generators when cyclic relationships exist among generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: TzSubstitute introduce new generator from word
rubrics_metrics.description: TzSubstitute(P, word) substitutes the given word as a new generator: it creates a new abstract generator g, adds it to P, and adds relator g^-1 * word. In the second form TzSubstitute(P[, n[, eliminate]]) substitutes a squarefree length-2 word as new generator and then eliminates a generator from the extended list; defaults: n=1, eliminate=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TzSubstitute first determines the n most frequently occurring relator subwords of the form g1g2 (g1,g2 different gens or inverses) and sorts them by decreasing occurrences — useful for selecting substitution candidates. Using substitute+eliminate can reduce total length at the cost of increasing generator count transiently.
